index.note: Flow opens the room: what the identity is and why it had to be tough, then two chapters that are also the section titles, the campaign pictures from a family trip to Big Bend and then the marks; the empty marks head is dropped and its chapter keys on the closing section, where the marks' pictures land, and the room ends on the scuffed boot. 8 Oct: his answers, nothing was shot for the campaign (the trip photographs were reused) and there is no apparel to show. The campaign chapter keys on "The campaign" so it holds before and after the head is patched.
index.stand: Brand identity for Capitan Boot Co., a Western boot maker: logo, type, badges, and campaign photography. | Capitan needed a brand that could take as much wear as its boots.

The campaign.t: The campaign uses photographs from a family trip to Big Bend,
The campaign.g: the landscape the boots are made for
li: The places | mesa country, river bottom, and grassland at last light.
The lockups | they sit right on top of the photographs.
When | the campaign came after the marks.

The same person drew the marks.t: The buffalo was drawn as a stamp first and an illustration second,
The same person drew the marks.g: since stamps blur and embossing flattens out
li: The bull skull | the lockup is drawn on a geometric grid, so the proportions stay put from a thumbnail stamp up to a banner.
The type | Northwest Regular and Oldman Regular, where Northwest carries the size and Oldman carries the character.
Small | the buffalo logo and the vintage badge, closer to the size they'd be on a hangtag.
The same person drew the marks.proof: Every color, typeface, and lockup was tested the way it would be produced before it went into the brand.

decks.The campaign: The same person drew the marks and shot the photographs.
